title: current-withdrawal-erases-historical-validity

proposition.statement: A relying system must not infer that an artifact or event was never valid merely because its authority, status, or availability was later withdrawn, revoked, or superseded.

preconditions: The artifact or event was valid under the applicable rules at historical time t1.
A later lifecycle event at time t2 changes its current status or availability.
A relying decision asks whether the artifact or event was valid at t1 rather than whether it is valid now.

trigger.statement: The relying system answers a historical-validity question using only the artifact's current withdrawn, revoked, or superseded state.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence of the artifact state at the historical time and the later lifecycle event.
Evidence distinguishing the historical verification time from the later lifecycle-event time.
Evidence of the rules governing historical validity for the relevant context.
Evidence sufficient to attribute historical and current state assertions to competent sources.

falsification.condition: The system concludes that the artifact was invalid at the historical time solely because it is withdrawn, revoked, or superseded now.
The system collapses current-state evidence and historical-state evidence into a single undifferentiated validity result.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the lifecycle failure tranche.
